chunks: I have come to know of words uttered by you which go in your favour as well as against you.
So, when my messenger reaches you prepare yourself and get ready, come out of your den and call those who are with you.
Then, if you are convinced of the truth get up but if you feel cowardice go away.

key_terms.مِئْزَرَكَ: your apron/girdle (symbolizing preparation or girding for action)

ai.seo_question: What did Ali (peace be upon him) instruct Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to do regarding his governance and conduct in Kufa?
ai.summary: This letter, part of Ali’s correspondence during the consolidation of Kufa, critiques Abu Musa al-Ash'ari for his perceived hesitation and lack of martial vigor in the face of external threats. The metaphorical commands to 'raise your hem' and 'exit your burrow' symbolize a call to shed passivity and assume active leadership, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *jihād al-akbar* (struggle) as both internal discipline and external political action. The concluding dichotomy—'if you are sincere, proceed; if you fail, withdraw'—underscores the principle of *ikhlas* (sincerity) in governance and military command.
